newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil basket falls for seventh week.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil basket falls for seventh week.

text.p: The average price of Venezuela's oil exports slid for a seventh week running to $16.95 per barrel on Friday, 17 cents below last Friday's figure, according to figures released by the Ministry of Energy and Mines.

The price has fallen by about 25 percent since the beginning of the year, when it reached a peak of $22.50 per barrel, and has been left behind by a recent recovery in the price of some other types of oil.
The world price of light, sweet crude oil touched a three- week high on Friday, but the recovery failed to spread to Venezuela's heavy, sour export prices.

International oil traders say sour crude prices have been dropping particularly fast because the big regional producers Canada, Mexico and Venezuela were all competing aggressively for U.S. market share in an oversupplied market.
The average Venezuelan basket price so far in March was $16.89 per barrel, compared to $18.78 average for the month of February and $21.53 per barrel in January, the official figures showed.

The average price for the year so far stood at $19.59 per barrel on Friday, against $19.88 last week. In 1996, the basket price averaged $18.39 per barrel, one of the highest in recent years, and well above the 1995 figure of $14.84 per barrel.
